security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick findings are false positives because they point to Markdown fences, inline identifiers, or prose. The semantic review found risk in unpinned npx execution and repeated instructions to run relative workspace scripts that perform writes. No prompt injection or data exfiltration language was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to a reviewed version and require confirmation before any npx command runs.

remediation.issue: Relative script execution without bundled scripts
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the referenced scripts or require users to inspect exact workspace scripts before execution.

remediation.issue: Repository write operations are described as automated steps
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run, explicit approval, and draft-only defaults for PR creation, releases, repository creation, and automated fixes.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs execution of npx claude-flow@alpha, which can fetch mutable package code during task execution. This creates supply-chain risk if a user or agent runs the command without verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The npx command is explicit and uses an alpha tag rather than a pinned version. Risk depends on runtime confirmation and trust in the external package.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Relative Script Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly directs agents to run relative bash scripts for cloning, pull requests, releases, repository creation, and automated fixes. The scanned skill contains only SKILL.md and multi-repo-process.dot, so matching workspace scripts could be executed instead.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions contain multiple explicit relative bash script invocations. The file structure for this skill does not include those scripts, increasing workspace-confusion risk.

content.value_statement: Multi-repository programs are difficult to change consistently across dependencies, CI, and releases. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured process for analysis, migration, enforcement, and synchronized delivery.
actual_capabilities: Defines a hierarchical agent workflow for coordinating changes across multiple repositories.
Maps repository dependencies and uses graph output to plan update order.
Guides monorepo migration into focused repositories while preserving Git history.
Coordinates synchronized pull requests, testing, versioning, and releases.
Describes architecture compliance scanning and remediation workflows.
Shows MCP tool calls for GitHub analysis and swarm task tracking.
limitations: It does not include the referenced shell scripts or templates.
It requires approved access to target repositories and GitHub tooling.
It cannot guarantee changes are correct without project tests and reviews.
It assumes teams can run MCP tools and external repository commands safely.

use_cases.title: Propagate Shared API Changes
use_cases.description: Plan and sequence updates when one service contract affects several dependent repositories.

use_cases.title: Split a Monorepo Safely
use_cases.description: Design target repositories, preserve history, update dependencies, and validate the cutover plan.

use_cases.title: Enforce Architecture Standards
use_cases.description: Scan related repositories for policy drift and create a coordinated remediation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Map Repository Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery for a small repository group.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these repositories and identify direct dependencies, shared packages, and likely update order. Return a short dependency map and review risks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cross-Repo Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a shared API or package change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a coordinated change plan for this API update across the affected repositories. Include sequencing, tests, owners, draft pull requests, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Monorepo Split
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration planning before repository creation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this monorepo structure and propose target repositories. Include module boundaries, dependency changes, history preservation, CI changes, and validation gates.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Synchronized Release
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release coordination across dependent repositories.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a synchronized release plan for these repositories. Include dependency order, version strategy, integration tests, merge rules, release notes, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Update a shared authentication API across five microservices.
output: The skill identifies upstream and downstream repositories before changes begin.
It proposes draft pull requests, integration tests, and merge order based on dependencies.
It highlights rollback tags and release notes needed for a coordinated deployment.

output_examples.input: Move three packages from a monorepo into separate repositories.
output: The skill outlines target repository boundaries and shared library strategy.
It includes history preservation, dependency rewrites, CI setup, and validation gates.
It separates planning tasks from repository write operations for review.

output_examples.input: Check whether service repositories follow the same architecture rules.
output: The skill creates a compliance workflow with rules, scan steps, and remediation priorities.
It groups violations by severity and assigns follow-up work by repository.
It recommends continuous checks after the initial cleanup.

best_practices: Review every generated plan before any repository write operation.
Run changes in dependency order and keep rollback tags for coordinated releases.
Use dry runs and draft pull requests before merges or releases.
anti_patterns: Do not run relative shell scripts from a workspace before reviewing their contents.
Do not merge downstream repositories before shared dependencies are released.
Do not let worker agents change repository architecture without coordinator review.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps plan coordinated work across related GitHub repositories, especially when dependencies and releases must stay aligned.

faq.question: Does it create repository changes automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflows that can lead to changes, but users should approve commands and review pull requests first.

faq.question: Can it migrate a monorepo into several repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes planning, repository creation, history preservation, dependency rewrites, and validation steps.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It references Claude Flow, Flow Nexus MCP tools, GitHub access, Graphviz, Git, and repository automation scripts.

faq.question: Is it suitable for small teams?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow supports two to five repositories and can scale to larger repository groups.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review repository access, external packages, shell scripts, write operations, and release permissions.
